description: Standardized data dictionary and evaluation criteria for the 14 Tailor2 blind human review dimensions.

factual_trustworthiness.name: Factual Trustworthiness & Provenance
factual_trustworthiness.description: Strict fidelity to canonical profile facts. The resume must contain zero fabricated employers, dates, degrees, metrics, or technical mechanisms.
factual_trustworthiness.evaluation_focus: Check if every bullet and skill claim is directly grounded in canonical experience. Watch for invented numbers, altered past job titles, or inflated scopes.
positive_indicators: All metrics match verified profile claims or accepted tolerances
Previous job titles and company names are reproduced verbatim without alterations
Technical mechanisms describe realistic, defensible engineering work
negative_indicators: Fabrication of metrics not present in master profile (e.g., turning 'improved latency' into 'improved latency by 92%')
Unauthorized alteration of former job title (e.g., changing 'Software Developer' to 'Backend Engineer' or dropping 'Intern')
Attributing tools or systems to employers where the candidate never used them

target_role_fit.name: Target Role Fit & Alignment
target_role_fit.description: Alignment with target job description requirements, core competencies, domain challenges, and tech stack.
target_role_fit.evaluation_focus: Assess whether the chosen bullets and highlighted strengths directly address the core challenges outlined in the JD.
positive_indicators: Bullets prioritize experience most relevant to the target role's tech stack and domain
Professional summary and skills sections align cleanly with job requirements
Demonstrates direct experience solving problems similar to the target team's responsibilities
negative_indicators: Irrelevant experience emphasized at the expense of directly applicable work
Missing obvious table-stakes technologies explicitly demanded by the JD
Reads as a generic resume without tailoring to the target role

recruiter_scan_quality.name: Recruiter Scan Quality (6-Second Test)
recruiter_scan_quality.description: Information architecture and visual skimmability for a fast recruiter scan.
recruiter_scan_quality.evaluation_focus: Determine if a recruiter can grasp candidate seniority, core stack, top achievements, and education within a 6-second initial scan.
positive_indicators: Strong action verbs lead each bullet point
Key technologies and metrics are placed early in bullets or easy to spot
Clean, consistent hierarchy (Company, Title, Dates, Location, Bullets)
negative_indicators: Dense walls of text that cause cognitive fatigue
Passive sentence structures ('Responsible for...', 'Assisted with...')
Burying key accomplishments at the end of lengthy, unstructured paragraphs

clarity.name: Clarity & Conciseness
clarity.description: Clear, precise communication free from ambiguity, convoluted syntax, and wordiness.
clarity.evaluation_focus: Evaluate sentence flow, grammatical precision, and whether complex technical ideas are expressed crisply.
positive_indicators: Crisp phrasing that communicates maximum impact with minimal words
Flawless grammar and punctuation
Unambiguous technical descriptions
negative_indicators: Run-on sentences and convoluted clauses
Filler words that add length without technical substance
Vague hand-waving descriptions of technical contributions

achievement_strength.name: Achievement & Impact Strength
achievement_strength.description: Emphasis on tangible technical and business outcomes rather than routine duty descriptions.
achievement_strength.evaluation_focus: Examine whether bullets demonstrate that the candidate delivered real value and measurable technical results.
positive_indicators: Accomplishment-oriented structure (Accomplished [X], as measured by [Y], by doing [Z])
Clear business or system-level impact (throughput, reliability, cost, adoption)
Highlights engineering ownership and problem-solving
negative_indicators: Pure chore or task logs ('Wrote unit tests', 'Attended daily standups')
Effort described without any outcome or impact
Weak, passive impact statements

metric_interpretability.name: Metric Interpretability & Credibility
metric_interpretability.description: Quantifiable figures that make logical engineering sense and carry meaningful context.
metric_interpretability.evaluation_focus: Verify that numbers and percentages are interpretable, plausible, and provide appropriate baseline or scale.
positive_indicators: Contextualized metrics (e.g., 'reduced p99 latency from 320ms to 45ms')
Scale and volume indicators that demonstrate production complexity (e.g., 'processing 10M daily events')
Credible, defensible orders of magnitude
negative_indicators: Meaningless standalone percentages ('improved efficiency by 40%' without saying what improved)
Implausible or impossible metrics (e.g., 'achieved 1000x speedup' on standard CRUD endpoint)
Metric stacking without engineering substance

interview_defensibility.name: Interview Defensibility
interview_defensibility.description: Whether claims can be vigorously defended under deep technical interrogation by senior interviewers.
interview_defensibility.evaluation_focus: Determine if the candidate can explain trade-offs, architectures, edge cases, and failure modes for everything claimed.
positive_indicators: Claims match standard engineering practices and architectures
Accurate terminology and architectural trade-offs reflect genuine hands-on experience
Defensible scope consistent with candidate's career level
negative_indicators: Buzzword dropping without coherent architectural context
Claims that suggest unrealistic senior architect authority for early-career projects
Superficial buzzword associations that fall apart under basic technical questioning

mechanism_outcome_balance.name: Mechanism-Outcome Balance (How vs. What)
mechanism_outcome_balance.description: Equal balance between technical mechanisms (how the problem was solved) and outcomes (what was achieved).
mechanism_outcome_balance.evaluation_focus: Check that bullets neither become pure implementation manuals nor pure management-summary fluff.
positive_indicators: Specific mechanisms mentioned (e.g., 'partition key redesign', 'eBPF probe', 'connection pooling')
Clear causal link between the mechanism employed and the resulting performance/reliability outcome
Balanced narrative in each bullet
negative_indicators: Overly technical implementation details with zero indication of why it mattered
Fluffy executive statements with no technical mechanism mentioned ('Transformed cloud ecosystem')
Disconnected claims where the mechanism cannot logically produce the stated outcome

redundancy.name: Redundancy & Repetition Avoidance
redundancy.description: Efficient use of bullet space without repeating action verbs, technologies, or themes across jobs.
redundancy.evaluation_focus: Assess whether bullet points offer diverse evidence across the candidate's full skillset rather than repeating the same story.
positive_indicators: Varied action verbs across all bullet openings
Each bullet demonstrates a distinct competency or architectural domain
Zero duplicate phrasing between summary, projects, and work history
negative_indicators: Opening 4+ bullets with 'Developed', 'Built', or 'Designed'
Repeating the exact same database optimization story in multiple roles
Redundant bullet points that rephrase the same achievement

ai_slop.name: Freedom from AI Slop & Clichés
ai_slop.description: Absence of stereotypical generative AI phrasing, hollow superlatives, and robotic cadence.
ai_slop.evaluation_focus: Watch for LLM hallmarks like 'spearheaded', 'orchestrated seamless transitions', 'tapestry', 'testament to', and breathless corporate jargon.
positive_indicators: Natural, authoritative engineering voice
Pragmatic, matter-of-fact tone
No hollow puffery or hyperbole
negative_indicators: Overused LLM tropes ('spearheaded multifaceted initiatives', 'leveraged cutting-edge synergies')
Unnatural uniform cadence across every single sentence
Overly dramatic descriptions of mundane software development tasks

skills_credibility.name: Skills Section Credibility
skills_credibility.description: Authentic, well-categorized technical skills that match the evidence presented in the experience bullets.
skills_credibility.evaluation_focus: Verify that listed technologies are backed up by actual project/work bullets and logically organized.
positive_indicators: Clean, logical taxonomy (e.g., Languages, Frameworks, Cloud & Distributed Systems, Databases)
Every major claimed skill is corroborated by experience bullets
Focused, credible list rather than encyclopedic kitchen-sink dump
negative_indicators: Claiming 40+ technologies without bullet corroboration
Listing outdated or trivial tools alongside core systems (e.g., 'JSON', 'Eclipse', 'Notepad')
Mismatched categorization (e.g., listing PostgreSQL under Languages)

visual_readability.name: Visual Readability & Typography
visual_readability.description: Professional typesetting, clean spacing, comfortable margins, and elimination of awkward line wraps.
visual_readability.evaluation_focus: Review layout cleanliness, bullet indentation, margins, font sizing, and ensure no orphaned words (widows) on trailing lines.
positive_indicators: Comfortable vertical line spacing and section breaks
Balanced margins (neither cramped nor excessive)
Bullet points wrap cleanly without single-word runover lines (widows)
negative_indicators: Cramped text that strains reader eyes
Ragged line wraps leaving a solitary word on a second line
Inconsistent indentation or misaligned date/location columns

page_utilization.name: Page Utilization & Budget Compliance
page_utilization.description: Exact 1-page budget compliance without spilling onto page 2 or leaving gaping bottom voids.
page_utilization.evaluation_focus: Check that the resume fills the single-page canvas naturally (85-98% vertical fill) without overflowing.
positive_indicators: Strictly 1 page with no spillover lines
Natural bottom margin (0.4in to 0.75in remaining whitespace)
Balanced density throughout all sections
negative_indicators: Spilling 1-3 lines onto a second page
Massive empty gap (more than 25% of page) at the bottom of the page
Extreme vertical squishing used to artificially force content onto 1 page

overall_preference.name: Overall Hiring Preference
overall_preference.description: The ultimate bottom-line hiring decision: which resume candidate would you submit to the hiring manager?
overall_preference.evaluation_focus: Weigh factual trustworthiness, target fit, recruiter appeal, and visual polish into a single definitive choice.
positive_indicators: Select candidate 'A' or 'B' based on superior overall candidate presentation
Select 'TIE' only if both resumes are virtually indistinguishable in quality and credibility
Select 'NEITHER' if both resumes exhibit fatal factual flaws or fail minimum acceptable hiring bar
negative_indicators: Selecting a candidate that contains fatal factual errors or resume fraud
Ignoring severe visual rendering failures in favor of content
